doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Fats Waller as influence and learning from other musicians
summary: He has loved Fats Waller since age nine and learned from players on all instruments.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now I know Fats Waller was an influence on your playing, is that a fair statement?
That’s right. Yeah, I’ve loved Fats from the beginning of my musical experience when I started at nine and he’ll be with me until I’m gone.
He wrote some great tunes too.
Oh, he was a wonderful musician. I always liked what Fats said, he said, “I was born balling, and I’m gonna have a ball as long as I live.”
What a character. Who else were some people you listened to and maybe grabbed a little bit of influence from?
Well I played with a lot of different guys that are gone now, they’ve died. But I’ve learned from so many of the guys on different instruments you know?
Yeah, that’s right, sure. You try to keep your ears open.
